name: Cellulite lasers / Cellfina

lead: Cellfina is a device-guided subcision procedure for dimple-type cellulite. Laser and other energy devices are discussed alongside it as options.
A pivotal study followed Cellfina patients for three years and reported sustained improvement; evidence for laser treatments is not covered in the available sources.

paras: Subcision releases the fibrous bands that tether the skin and create dimples; Cellfina does this with a tissue-stabilized, guided device.

It is a minimally invasive in-office procedure; clinicians note patient selection matters because not all body contour concerns are dimple-type cellulite. Complication data are not detailed in the sources reviewed.

lead: Cellulite lasers and Cellfina are in-office procedures aimed at the dimpled skin surface that many people, mostly women, notice on the thighs and buttocks. Cellfina is a tissue-stabilized, guided subcision device that mechanically releases the fibrous bands under the skin that are associated with dimple-type cellulite [1][2]. Laser and other energy-based devices are a separate group of treatments that are discussed alongside it [3].

In looksmaxxing communities the topic sits at the edge of body-focused hardmaxxing, and the available published research comes from the dermatology literature rather than from forums. A pivotal open-label multicenter study followed Cellfina patients for three years and reported sustained improvement in the appearance of cellulite [1]. Treatment authors also note that the device is best suited to dimple-type cellulite and that patients often label other body features as cellulite [2].

paras: Cellulite is a common cosmetic concern in women, and a 2017 pivotal-study paper described no single treatment as having been proven effective over the long term before the tissue stabilized-guided subcision (TS-GS) system appeared [1]. Wikipedia lists laser and pulsed-light treatments, subcision, radiofrequency, ultrasound, cryotherapy and collagenase injections among options used, and notes that cellulite can be resistant to many treatments [3].

Subcision cuts the fibrous bands that pull on the skin surface. It can be done manually, with vacuum assistance, or with laser assistance [3]. Cellfina is the first FDA-cleared, long-lasting, minimally invasive device for improving cellulite appearance, according to a Canadian retrospective evaluation [4].

Clinicians who have shared their experience with Cellfina say it most effectively treats dimple-type cellulite, where fibrous bands inserting into the underside of the skin create a puckered look, and that prospective patients should be educated about this because many consider any undesirable feature from the knees to the umbilicus to be cellulite [2].
A multicenter pivotal study of the TS-GS system reported significant reductions in the appearance of cellulite and extended follow-up out to three years after the initial treatment [1].

A multicenter retrospective evaluation from two early Canadian sites looked at efficacy and patient satisfaction in the first year the device was on the market in Canada [4]. A registered trial of a different device, the Cabochon system, enrolled 55 participants beginning in 2012 for cellulite appearance [5]. The sources available do not provide results for laser treatments specifically.

Wikipedia reports that cellulite affects a large majority of post-adolescent women of European descent and is considerably less common in East Asian women, and that the term originated in spa and beauty services in the 1920s. A 1978 paper called it an invented disease [3].
